title: A big festival day in Thatcham
summary: Saturday saw a number of events attracting local people as as part of Thatcham Town Council's annual festival festival where the best of Thatcham was on show.
imageAlt: Celia Camplin displays her hand knitted animals for sale
caption: A lady stood by a table packed with knitted animal toys, which she is offering for sale

content.text:
Saturday was a big day in Thatcham as events ran across the town by organisations showcasing the best of what they do.

St Mary's Church was a popular venue where over a hundred people came to buy from the many stalls at the craft fair, listen to the music, and enjoy a cup of tea and a cake. Mrs. Celia Camplin, (pictured above), was one of the many stalleholders offering her products to the visitors who came along. She had a wide collection of hand-knitted animals for sale.

the Thatcham Historical Society were also present at the church, where members were displaying pictures and educating visitors about the history of Thatcham from the evidence of the very earliest prehistoric life forms, the earliest human settlements through to the modern town that Thatcham is today.

content.imageAlt: The Thatcham Historical Society stand at St Mary's Church during the Thatcham Festival
content.caption: Visitors to the Thatcham Historical Society learn about the interesting history of Thatcham

content.text: Elsewhere in the town, an event was held, looking at the historical and modern uses of different plants. The 'Herbal Histories' event in the Jubilee Sensory Garden next to the Thatcham Town Council offices gave visitors the opportunity to join a walk and talk around the Sensory Garden and to learn how to make an herbal balm to take home.

content.imageAlt: A picture of a raised box containing various plants at the Jubilee Sensory Garden
content.caption: Jubilee Sensory Garden

content.text: the Broadway was busy and was taken over by local clubs and societies, showcasing what they do and hoping to recruit some new members
